sections.title: Five pure sounds
sections.content: Spanish has just five vowel sounds, and each one is always pronounced the same way, wherever it appears: a ("ah"), e ("eh"), i ("ee"), o ("oh"), u ("oo"). English vowels tend to glide — the "o" in "go" actually slides from "oh" toward "oo" as you say it. Spanish vowels don't glide at all: hold the sound flat and steady from start to finish.

This is the single biggest thing that marks an English accent in Spanish: gliding a vowel that should stay flat. Say *no* like the English word "no" and it comes out as two sounds, "noh-oo" — say it like Spanish *no* and it's one clean sound held to the end, no drift.
